notes.summary: An average is the total of the values divided by how many values there are. SSC asks about 1 question in Tier 1 and 1 to 2 in Tier 2, usually on people joining, leaving or being replaced, wrong entries, consecutive numbers and cricket. Nearly all of them reduce to one rule: sum = average × number.

concepts.title: What an average is
concepts.body:
Average = Sum of values ÷ Number of values. So Sum = Average × Number. Almost every average question is solved by turning averages into sums.

Example: the average of 5 numbers is 27, so their sum is 135. If one is removed and the other 4 average 25 (sum 100), the removed number is 35.

The average always lies between the smallest and the largest value.

concepts.title: Assumed average (deviation method)
concepts.body:
Guess a round value close to the numbers, find how far each number is from it, and correct the guess.

Average = Assumed value + (sum of deviations) ÷ n

Example: 47, 52, 49, 55, 47. Assume 50. Deviations: −3, +2, −1, +5, −3. Sum = 0. Average = 50.

This also explains every shortcut below: the average moves by (total extra) ÷ (number of values).

concepts.title: Changing every value
concepts.body:
• Add k to every value: the average increases by k.
  • Subtract k from every value: the average decreases by k.
  • Multiply every value by k: the average is multiplied by k.
  • Divide every value by k: the average is divided by k.

Example: the average of 8 numbers is 25. Each is increased by 4 and then doubled. New average = (25 + 4) × 2 = 58.

concepts.title: Averages of number patterns
concepts.body:
For numbers in arithmetic progression (equal gaps), average = (first + last) ÷ 2, which is also the middle term.

NumbersAverage
First n natural numbers(n + 1)/2
First n even numbersn + 1
First n odd numbersn
Squares of first n natural numbers(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6
Cubes of first n natural numbersn(n + 1)²/4
First n multiples of kk(n + 1)/2

Examples: average of the first 91 even numbers = 92. Average of the cubes of 1 to 5 = 5 × 36/4 = 45. Average of the first 20 multiples of 7 = 7 × 21/2 = 73.5.

concepts.title: Consecutive numbers
concepts.body:
For an odd count of consecutive numbers, the average is the middle number. For an even count, it is the mean of the two middle numbers.

  • 7 consecutive odd numbers with average 33: middle is 33, so the numbers are 27, 29, 31, 33, 35, 37, 39.
  • 8 consecutive odd numbers with average 28: middle two are 27 and 29, so smallest = 21, largest = 35, and smallest + largest = 56 = 2 × 28.
  • Sum of the smallest and largest = 2 × average, always.

concepts.title: Average of combined groups
concepts.body:
Combined average = (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂). Do not just average the two averages unless the groups are the same size.

Example: 60 students, 40% girls. 24 girls average 55 kg and 36 boys average 62 kg. Class average = (1320 + 2232)/60 = 59.2 kg.

To find the group sizes from the overall average, use alligation: n₁ : n₂ = (a₂ − A) : (A − a₁).

concepts.title: A member joins or leaves
concepts.body:
Group of n with average A.

  • One person joins and the average rises by d: new person = A + (n + 1)d. (If it falls, d is negative.)
  • One person leaves and the average rises by d: person who left = A − (n − 1)d.
  • Think of it as: the newcomer brings the old average for himself, plus d for every member of the new group.

Example: 30 students average 15 years; with the teacher the average is 16. Teacher = 15 + 31 × 1 = 46 years.

Example: 120 staff average 62.5 kg; one leaves and the average falls by 0.25 kg. Leaver = 62.5 + 119 × 0.25 = 92.25 kg.

concepts.title: Replacement
concepts.body:
When one member is replaced and the group size stays n:

New member = Old member + n × (change in average)

Example: the average weight of 8 persons rises by 2.5 kg when a 65 kg person is replaced. New person = 65 + 8 × 2.5 = 85 kg.

If the average falls, the new member is lighter: subtract instead. If two members are replaced, use their total.

concepts.title: Wrong entries
concepts.body:
Correct average = Wrong average + (correct values − wrong values) ÷ n

Example: average of 40 students was 68, but 84 and 46 were entered as 48 and 64. Correction = (130 − 112)/40 = 0.45. Correct average = 68.45.

Digit swaps: if 47 was read as 74, the sum went up by 27 and the average must come down by 27/n.

concepts.title: Overlapping groups
concepts.body:
When the first few and the last few numbers share a number, that common number is counted twice.

Common number = (sum of first group) + (sum of last group) − (total sum)

Example: 11 numbers average 50; the first 6 average 49 and the last 6 average 52. Sixth number = 294 + 312 − 550 = 56.

When the groups do not overlap, the leftover numbers = total sum − sums of the groups. Then use the extra conditions (for example, the 10th is 3 more than the 9th) to split the leftover.

concepts.title: Cricket: batting average and run rate
concepts.body:
• Batting average = total runs ÷ innings (completed innings). Bowling average = runs given ÷ wickets taken.
  • A batsman scores S in his nth innings and his average rises by d: new average = S − (n − 1)d. With 90 in the 12th innings and a rise of 5, new average = 90 − 55 = 35.
  • Run rate = runs ÷ overs. Required run rate = (target − runs made) ÷ overs left. 72 runs in 10 overs, target 272 in 50 overs: (272 − 72)/40 = 5.

concepts.title: Average age over time
concepts.body:
• After t years every person is t years older, so the average age of a fixed group also rises by t.
  • t years ago the average was t less.
  • When a child is born or someone joins, use totals: total now = average × number of people.
  • Example: husband and wife averaged 23 years at marriage. Five years later they have a 1-year-old child. Total = 46 + 10 + 1 = 57, average = 19 years.

varieties.name: Basic average and sums
varieties.how: Change every average into a sum (average × count). Add or subtract sums, then divide. If every value is changed the same way, change the average the same way.

example.q: The average of 8 numbers is 25. Each number is increased by 4 and then multiplied by 2. What is the new average?
steps: Adding 4 to each raises the average to 29.

varieties.name: Consecutive numbers and first n numbers
varieties.how: For consecutive numbers the average is the middle term. For first n numbers use the table: natural (n + 1)/2, even n + 1, odd n.

example.q: The average of five consecutive even numbers is 46. What is the product of the smallest and the largest?

varieties.name: Average of combined groups
varieties.how: Combined average = total of all sums ÷ total people. To find group sizes, use alligation: n₁ : n₂ = (a₂ − A) : (A − a₁).

example.q: The average salary of all workers in a factory is ₹8,000. The 20 officers average ₹15,000 and the other workers average ₹6,000. How many other workers are there?

varieties.name: A member joins or leaves
varieties.how: New total minus old total gives the person or group that joined. Shortcut for one joiner: old average + (new count) × rise.

example.q: The average weight of 24 students is 40 kg. When 6 new students join, the average becomes 41 kg. What is the average weight of the new students?

varieties.name: One member replaced by another
varieties.how: New member = old member + (group size × change in average). Use minus if the average falls.

example.q: The average weight of 10 persons increases by 1.5 kg when one of them weighing 58 kg is replaced by a new person. Find the new person’s weight.

varieties.name: Wrong entry corrected
varieties.how: Correct average = wrong average + (correct values − wrong values) ÷ n.

example.q: The average of 25 numbers is 36. Later it was found that 47 was read as 74. Find the correct average.

varieties.name: Overlapping parts of a list
varieties.how: Common number = sum of first group + sum of last group − total sum.

example.q: The average of 11 numbers is 50. The average of the first six is 49 and of the last six is 52. Find the sixth number.
steps: Sum of first six = 294, last six = 312, all eleven = 550.
The sixth number is counted twice.

varieties.name: Batting average and run rate
varieties.how: New average = score in the latest innings − (earlier innings × rise). Required run rate = runs still needed ÷ overs left.

example.q: A batsman scores 90 runs in his 12th innings and his average increases by 5. What is his average after the 12th innings?

varieties.name: Average age
varieties.how: Turn average ages into total ages. Add t years for each person for every t years that pass, and add new members’ ages.

example.q: At the time of marriage, the average age of a husband and wife was 23 years. Five years later they have a 1-year-old child. What is the average age of the family now?
steps: Total at marriage = 46; five years later = 46 + 10 = 56.

tips: Always turn averages into sums first. Sum = average × number.
Joiner = old average + (new count × rise). Replacement = old member + (count × rise).
For consecutive numbers, the average is the middle number.
Use an assumed average to add long lists of close numbers quickly.
For two groups, alligation gives the ratio of group sizes at once.
Over t years the average age of the same people rises by exactly t.
traps: Do not average two averages directly unless both groups are the same size.
When a teacher is included, the new count is n + 1, not n.
In replacement, the group size does not change; in joining, it does.
In cricket questions, the rise in average applies to the earlier innings, so use (n − 1), not n.
With overlapping groups, the shared number is counted twice; subtract the total once.

questions.q: What is the average of the first 10 natural numbers?
The average of 5 numbers is 27. If one number is excluded, the average of the remaining numbers becomes 25. What is the excluded number?
questions.solution:
Total of 5 numbers = 5 × 27 = 135.
Total of 4 numbers = 4 × 25 = 100.
Excluded number = 135 − 100 = 35.

questions.q: The average age of 30 students in a class is 15 years. When the teacher’s age is included, the average becomes 16 years. What is the teacher’s age?
questions.solution:
Total for students = 30 × 15 = 450.
Total with teacher = 31 × 16 = 496.
Teacher’s age = 496 − 450 = 46 years.

questions.q: The average of 7 consecutive odd numbers is 33. What is the largest of these numbers?
A batsman scores 87 runs in his 17th innings and thereby increases his average by 3. What is his average after the 17th innings?
questions.solution:
Let the average after 16 innings be x.
16x + 87 = 17(x + 3) → x = 87 − 51 = 36.
New average = 36 + 3 = 39.

questions.q: The average weight of 8 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person comes in place of one of them weighing 65 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.solution:
Increase in total = 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg.
New person = 65 + 20 = 85 kg.
